the components of commitment to organizational change combine to predict support for a change.

the development and validation of a measure of commitment to organizational change and the examination of how commitment to a change relates to support for the change and to organizational commitment.
the development and testing of a new measure of commitment to organizational change and its relationship to organizational change support behavior.
the development and application of a three-component model of commitment in the context of organizational change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
commitment to a change can be viewed as a multidimensional concept, and it can be differentiated from organizational commitment.
commitment to organizational change is a multidimensional concept that is best represented by a three-component model.
affective commitment to a change, and normative commitment are positively related to behavioral commitment to a change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three components of commitment to organizational change are distinct, but that they combine to predict behavior.
commitment to change, as conceptualized and measured in this study, is a multidimensional construct that is associated with behavioral support for organizational change.

affective, continuance, and normative commitment are distinct components of commitment to change that are associated with different behaviors and that the combination of all three components is a stronger predictor of behavior than any one of the components alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
employees’ commitment to change is an important predictor of behavior, and that it is best understood by considering the three components of commitment: affective, continuance, and normative.
commitment to a change, as measured by our three component model of commitment, can be used to predict support for change.

the three component model of commitment can be extended to the domain of commitment to organizational change, and that the three components of commitment to change have differential implications for support for change.
